tasks.title: Compose E2E accepts both API generations and proves database check persistence
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, all Behavior items 1-7, Checks 1-4 and Completion evidence Runs A/B; Security impact for E2E credentials and unchanged pins. Keep this one cohesive change to the existing scenario and its four supporting docs/comments. Detect the API kind exactly once using GET /admin/config with jq has(file) and has(shadowed); neither pins nor environment select a path. Retain shared CRUD/probe/status steps and use the literal create count for each path. Add database-only scenarios 3a-3e in their specified order: unchanged checks.json hash across CRUD; e2e-db-post POST with the specified literal Authorization, Content-Type, body and /status assertion, an up result, keep markers in the admin view and literal values preserved in probes after a name-only PUT; file shadow wins, database entry remains shadowed, PUT 409, restore unshadows; broken bytes { persist across POST 201/DELETE 204 with a fresh revision fetched per request, repair sets ok; e2e-db-keep survives down/up with source database. Use the section's literal ids, names, target URL, token fallback and body as expectations rather than fetched values. For Behavior item 4, use the secondary API on port 3999 and this exact database-path sequence: GET /admin/config, POST a valid check with that revision for 201, GET /admin/config again, POST a valid component with the newly fetched revision for 503. Required behavior 21 advances the generation on the 201; never reuse its consumed revision. The expected 201 and 503 are literals, and 412 at either request fails this step. Older API retains its existing read-only 503 case. Keep admin-token log absence and add svc-token absence after the database scenarios; never print credentials. Document writable-directory requirements separately for the pinned older API and the database-check API (components/windows still need it). Change no pin, image line or unrelated step. Run A uses the untouched pin; Run B builds the merged api main SHA and selects its image only in a disposable deploy copy, shows compose's selected image, runs all scenarios and deletes the copy. Record actual api SHA/image ID, both runs' ok lines and all checks for the PR. If detection/database scenarios already exist, follow the section's needs-input condition. If Run B fails outside this scope, hold needs-input naming the step; report unavailable Docker evidence honestly. Keep feature detection, all database cases and both acceptance runs in this one task: they exercise one existing E2E scenario, and the other four files only explain its mount behavior. This task follows the merged api, whose console compatibility has already been verified by API Check 10; the deploy console image pin stays unchanged.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; every E2E helper test of CI job lint passes.
exit 0; all static setups pass and malformed setup fixtures are rejected.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; all remaining script tests of CI job lint pass, including the Docker secrets-init checks.
exit 0; repository lint, typecheck and full CLI tests pass.

acceptance.command: git diff --exit-code "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)" HEAD -- common/services.yaml
acceptance.expected: exit 0; no committed pin or shared image changed.

Run A in the unchanged-pin checkout (api 0.1.0) exits 0 and ends ==> All checks passed; output includes ok: the api writes admin checks to the file (older api) and ok: the read-only mount answers 503. Existing create counter is the literal count 1 at its check; no database-only scenario runs.

acceptance.command: docker build -t pulse-api:e2e-<sha> <api checkout at sha>
acceptance.expected: Run B preparation succeeds for the recorded merged api main SHA; record its image ID and use this tag only in the disposable deploy copy required by the section.
In the disposable Run B deploy copy, the selected api image is pulse-api:e2e-<recorded merged api SHA>; the only temporary image edit is common/services.yaml's api image value.

Run B in that copy exits 0 and ends ==> All checks passed; output includes ok: the api stores admin checks in the database and ok lines for 3a-3e and 4. File hash stays equal across CRUD. e2e-db-post has an up result, admin headers.Authorization and body equal {keep:true}, and after the name-only PUT its probe Authorization equals Bearer plus the scenario's E2E_SVC_TOKEN value (fallback e2e-svc-token-sentinel) and its body equals the literal {"ping":"e2e-body-sentinel"}. Shadow name is E2E file shadow with PUT 409 then database restoration; broken bytes { survive POST 201 and DELETE 204, each using a freshly fetched revision; repaired state is ok; e2e-db-keep persists with source database. On the secondary read-only API at port 3999, GET /admin/config immediately before the valid check POST (literal 201), then GET /admin/config again immediately before the valid component POST (literal 503). The second GET must happen after the check POST succeeds; 412 from either POST fails this acceptance step. Admin/svc tokens are absent from logs and never printed. Use literal per-path create counts. Delete the disposable copy after recording evidence.

PR lists #565, merged api SHA and image ID, both runs' actual ok lines and Checks 1-4 results, plus the security review of credential redaction, no secret output, unchanged pins and limited scope. Any unavailable Docker evidence is explicitly reported; an unrelated Run B failure causes needs-input naming the step.
